note: Two additional image paths referenced by the same create-manage-roles doc (media/create-manage-roles/data-access.png and media/create-manage-roles/members-in-role.png) consistently returned HTTP 200 with Content-Type: text/html (an empty/placeholder page, not an image) under curl -sI, including with a browser user-agent — a genuine dead-link gap in Microsoft's own docs media folder, not a search shortfall. Two other candidate images (media/row-level-security/select-row-security.png, media/column-level-security/select-column-security.png) verified as real image/png but cover row-level/column-level security, which this lesson only references in passing (it's detailed in a later lesson), so they were left unused rather than padding the lesson with off-topic screenshots. The 4 screenshots used clear the 3-screenshot floor and walk the full role lifecycle: create and scope -> verify scope -> assign members -> edit later. All UI details (role names like 'OneLakeSecurityRole'/'SampleRole', table/folder names like 'publicholidays', 'images', 'sample_datasets', wizard step order, DefaultReader behavior, virtual membership permissions list) were read directly off the fetched Microsoft Learn pages, not inferred.
